stem: A retail CDTM agreement and patient referral cover diabetes management only. The same patient asks the collaborating pharmacist to issue a new warfarin prescription for atrial fibrillation and promises that the pharmacist can send a copy to the supervising physician within 24 hours. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: The 24-hour copy requirement by itself authorizes any Schedule VI prescription for that patient.
Sending a timely copy does not expand CDTM prescribing beyond the referred diagnosis and agreement scope.
Warfarin is Schedule II, so the request is barred solely by federal Schedule II refill law.
The request becomes authorized if the patient signs a second consent without a new referral or agreement scope.
The pharmacist may issue the prescription first and decide afterward whether atrial fibrillation was covered.

explanation.core_reasoning: The retail CDTM Schedule VI prescribing authority is tied to the referred diagnosis and the collaborative agreement. The separate duty to transmit a copy to the supervising physician within 24 hours is a follow-up obligation, not a device for expanding scope.

choice_analysis.A: Timely communication is required when authorized prescribing occurs, but it does not create authority for an unrelated diagnosis.
choice_analysis.B: The proposed warfarin prescription falls outside the stated diabetes referral and agreement even if the copy would be sent on time.
choice_analysis.C: Warfarin is not federal Schedule II; the decisive problem is the CDTM scope described in the stem.
choice_analysis.D: Patient consent cannot substitute for the physician-pharmacist agreement and referral boundaries.
choice_analysis.E: Scope must exist before the pharmacist exercises the special prescribing authority.

related_facts: Massachusetts Schedule VI prescribing can be part of retail CDTM when the statutory conditions are met.
A copy of an authorized pharmacist-issued prescription must be sent to the supervising physician within the required period.
explanation.mpje_trap: Documentation after an act does not create authority that was missing before the act.

reasoning_steps: Classify warfarin as a Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription drug
Compare the requested indication with the referral and agreement
Treat the 24-hour copy duty as a follow-up requirement rather than a source of authority
